extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and scholars interested in peer review, scientific bias, and experimental psychology
extracted.subtask_description: An experimental study examining how reviewers' theoretical perspectives and the direction of reported results (positive/negative/mixed/none) influence manuscript evaluations, producing findings about bias and interrater agreement in journal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmatory bias (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Confirmatory bias is the tendency to emphasize and believe experiences which support one's views and to ignore or discredit those which do not."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as a documented tendency in clinical research; the paper treats this psychological tendency as a potential influence on the behavior of scientists and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reported results on review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers were asked to referee manuscripts which described identical experimental procedures but which reported positive, negative, mixed, or no results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study manipulates only the reported outcome to test how the direction/valence of findings affects reviewers' judgments; implies that identical methods can be judged differently depending on result direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias against manuscripts contrary to reviewers' theoretical perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers were strongly biased against manuscripts which reported results contrary to their theoretical perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a central empirical finding with direct implications for publication decisions; suggests that congruence with a reviewer's theoretical commitments influences accept/reject recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor interrater agreement among reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to showing poor interrater agreement, reviewers were strongly biased ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports low consistency between reviewers assessing the same (but outcome-varied) manuscripts, indicating limited reliability of peer review judgments in the study context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication as determinant of scientific contribution and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication is a critical element in determining the contribution and impact of scientific findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to motivate why biases in review (e.g., confirmatory bias) matter—because they can shape which findings are published and therefore perceived as contributing to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of investigating variables operative in journal review policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Little research attention has been devoted to the variables operative in journal review policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper positions its experiment as addressing these understudied variables (e.g., reported result direction, reviewer theoretical perspective) and implies these are meaningful dimensions that affect review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for epistemology and the peer review system
rubrics_metrics.description: The implications of these findings for epistemology and the peer review system are briefly addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings are framed not just as descriptive (that bias exists) but as having normative/epistemic consequences for how knowledge is validated and circulated through publication practices.
